title: Permissive-Operator Surcharge on Total Losses Paid to a Loss Payee
content:
Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), a permissive-operator surcharge is added to the deductible carried by the vehicle value paid to a loss payee.

**Who was operating, and what was the cause?**
- A permissive user who does not live in the household was the operator recorded on the claim report, and the cause is a collision: the permissive-collision surcharge of 500 USD is added.
- That operator was such a permissive user and the cause is comprehensive: the permissive-comprehensive surcharge of 250 USD is added.
- Any other operator: no surcharge.

**Does a rated household driver bring a surcharge?** No. Nor does a named excluded driver, an unlisted household resident, or a parked-vehicle loss with no driver.

**Hypothetical: a visiting cousin totals the car in a collision.** The cousin does not live in the household, so 500 USD is added to the deductible. Had the car been flooded while the cousin had it, 250 USD would be added.
